profile.name: Lungi Panchi Dance
profile.tagline: A traditional dance of the Santal people in West Bengal.
profile.insight: Female dancers perform in a line holding hands, while men provide the musical accompaniment using traditional drums like the madal and lagra.
profile.profile: The Lungi Panchi Dance is a traditional performance style practiced by the Santal people of West Bengal. It is characterized by the coordinated movement of female dancers in a line, accompanied by male musicians playing traditional instruments. The dance takes its name from the specific attire worn by the women during the performance.
profile.profile_long:
The Lungi Panchi Dance is a traditional dancing style of the Santal people, an ethnic group with a significant presence in West Bengal, India, as well as in Bangladesh and Nepal. The dance is performed by both men and women, with distinct roles for each group. The name of the dance is derived from the clothing worn by the female participants, who typically dress in a lungi-panchi or a red-bordered white sari. Male dancers, by contrast, wear a dhoti and incorporate natural accessories into their performance, including turbans, tree leaves, flowers, and bushes.

A notable feature of the Lungi Panchi dance is the harmony of movement. Female dancers stand in a line, holding hands, and move to the rhythm of the music. While the women perform the dance, the men provide the musical accompaniment. The musical ensemble utilizes a variety of traditional instruments, including the madal, flute, dhamsa, jhanj, kartal, and the shehnai. Men and boys specifically use two types of drums, the madal and the lagra, to drive the rhythm of the performance.

The origins of the Lungi Panchi dance are described as unclear in available documentation. Some traditional beliefs suggest an origin in 1955, though this is linked in source material to a debated history involving the mixing of merengue and conga rhythms in Cuba. The Santal people, who perform this dance, are primarily an agricultural community, though many also work in plantations, factories, coal mines, and as port workers. The dance remains a component of the cultural life of the Santal community, which maintains remnants of primitive communal relations within their social system.
